clue.text: Long narrative again provided by Indian chief

parts.note: a saga is a long story of heroic deeds or family history
more, as in 'once more', means again

explanation.surface: A storyteller retells an epic in the presence of a tribal leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagamore is a chief among some Algonquian peoples of North America, a title close to sachem.

clue.text: Picking us up, heading off home perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top
the heading, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: in The Times crossword, 'us' is the newspaper itself

explanation.surface: Someone collects us and then sets off home.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's paper speaks: 'us' is THE TIMES's name, TIMES. 'heading off' leaves IMES, and 'up' (with 'Picking') turns it to SEMI. A semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi, short for semi-detached house, is one example of a house to live in.

clue.text: Costliest purge, I suspect, is a way to please some of the voters

definitions.text: a way to please some of the voters

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means doubtful, so these letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A politician suspects that an expensive clear-out will win over part of the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges COSTLIEST, PURGE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Gesture politics is action taken for show, to win public approval rather than to achieve much.

clue.text: Boss in red-top office reflected

parts.note: the Daily Mirror is a red-top, a British tabloid with a red masthead
the editor, ED, is the boss in a newspaper office

explanation.surface: The editor in a tabloid's office looked back thoughtfully.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid newspaper, named for its red title; the Mirror is one. ED, the editor, is the boss there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mirrored is shown back as an image, as light is reflected.

clue.text: In official costume, run carrying weight, not getting to the finish

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: obese means carrying a lot of excess weight

explanation.surface: A fat official in ceremonial dress tries to run but gives up before the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting to the finish' drops the final E of OBESE, leaving OBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Robes are the long formal garments worn by judges, clergy and dignitaries.

clue.text: It's right for individual to let go of son

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons

indicators.note: letting go of something drops it, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: a person is an individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone argues it is only fair for a man to release his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; the surface's father letting go of his boy hides a deletion of the word son from a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and right are synonyms, both meaning correct or fitting.

clue.text: Someone selling amateur recording

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, sells
lay means not professional, as in a layman

explanation.surface: A salesperson's home-made tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a playback of a recorded sequence, as in a sports action replay.

clue.text: On office desk you may find that perennials perch precariously

definitions.text: On office desk you may find that

indicators.note: perching precariously suggests a wobbly, disordered arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Potted plants balance on the edge of an office desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precariously' rearranges PERENNIALS and PERCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil sharpener is a common item of office stationery kept on desks.

clue.text: Orange and reds could make for pretty backyard

indicators.note: the letters could be remade into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Orange and red flowers would brighten a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make for' rearranges ORANGE and REDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose garden is a plot planted with roses, a pretty kind of garden behind a house.

clue.text: Faithful servant makes any number of pounds for trader

indicators.note: the first letter is made into the second, so one swaps for the other

parts.note: a retainer is a servant long attached to a household
N stands for any number in algebra
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A loyal servant earns a fortune working for a merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes any number of pounds' changes the N in RETAINER into L.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer sells goods to the public, a trader in shops.

clue.text: Note monarch in black, sorrowful

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the monarch sits inside the word for black

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A mournful message about a king dressed in mourning black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'black' look like the start of a funeral notice; each is a synonym piece, and ER is the usual crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable and sorrowful both describe a person weighed down by unhappiness.

clue.text: Drinks assigned marks (zero not given)

indicators.note: something not given is withheld, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: marks awarded in a test or contest are points
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A pub quiz where drinks are handed out as prizes, but nobody scores nil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not given' takes the O (zero) out of POINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a standard measure of beer in a British pub, so pints are drinks.

clue.text: Goddess in boat with love for king

indicators.note: one letter standing in for another means a swap

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A goddess sails in a boat, trading her love for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with love for king' swaps the K of JUNK for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Juno was the queen of the Roman gods, wife of Jupiter.

clue.text: Those afar in Grenada some as sailors

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: People living far away on the Caribbean island of Grenada are a nation of mariners.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafaring describes those who travel by sea, the way of life of sailors; the clue's 'as sailors' frames the adjective.

clue.text: God bearing fruit in magnificent manifestation

indicators.note: the inner pieces sit inside the word for magnificent

parts.note: ace means excellent or magnificent

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the god holds the fruit within

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A god carrying fruit appears in a splendid vision.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'bearing' has the god carry the fruit, and 'in' then sets the result inside the word for magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: An appearance is the act of becoming visible, a manifestation.

clue.text: About to have egg producers in large building, making a clutch possible

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the word for a large building

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
re means about, as in business letters
hens lay eggs

explanation.surface: A plan for a battery farm in a big barn, where a clutch of eggs can be laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' looks like a nest of eggs, given the hens, but means grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehensile tail or limb can grasp objects, so it makes gripping possible.

clue.text: Label in bank maybe to show deficit

indicators.note: the label is placed inside the word for the bank

parts.note: a shore is one kind of bank, of a sea or lake
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A tag on a bank statement shows the account is in the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' pretends to be the money kind; it is the land beside water.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack of something needed, a deficit.

clue.text: Druggie one who thinks head will float off

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word, drifts away and is lost

parts.note: a muser is someone who muses, that is thinks

explanation.surface: An addict imagining that his head is drifting away while high.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes drugs habitually.

clue.text: It's horrible, leader not being seen or properly recognised

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, is not seen and so drops away

parts.note: frightful means horrible

explanation.surface: It's awful that the boss is never seen or given due credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader not being seen' removes the F from FRIGHTFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rightful heir or owner is one legitimately acknowledged, so properly recognised.

clue.text: Biblical land way back

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word from its end

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A Bible land from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Edom was a kingdom south of the Dead Sea in the Old Testament, home of Esau's descendants.

clue.text: Harmonise with new decoration

indicators.note: making the letters new means arranging them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Matching up the colours with fresh décor.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate things is to bring them into agreement, which is what harmonising does.

clue.text: Tom's a bit confused inside — one going this way and that?

definitions.text: one going this way and that?

indicators.note: a slight muddle in the middle shifts one interior letter

parts.note: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero, so Tom's surname is Sawyer

explanation.surface: Tom is a little muddled within and staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit confused inside' moves the W of SAWYER one place forward, swapping the middle pair to make SWAYER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sways rocks from side to side, going one direction and then the other.

clue.text: Terrain was almost cracking — need for this?

definitions.text: Terrain was almost cracking — need for this?

indicators.note: cracking breaks the letters up so they re-form
almost means the word stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: Drought-cracked ground cries out for a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the S of 'was'; 'cracking' rearranges TERRAIN and WA. The whole clue is the definition: parched, cracking land needs what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched earth needs the water that falls from the sky in a shower.

clue.text: Stick used by one laying down the line

definitions.meaning: a stick here is a straight measuring rod for drawing lines
someone who governs sets the line, the policy others must follow

explanation.surface: A cane wielded by a strict teacher enforcing discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight measuring rod is used to draw lines, and a monarch sets the official policy, the line others follow.

clue.text: The fellow without work, and the virtue he needs?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the fellow wraps around the work

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a fellow
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An unemployed man and the virtue he needs to get through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The question mark admits that the definition reads off the surface of a jobless man.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is one of the three theological virtues, with faith and charity, and the jobless man needs optimism.

clue.text: Bird to sink down gripping end of branch

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bird drops down while clutching the tip of a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts H, the end of 'branch', inside SAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The shag is a European cormorant, a dark seabird.

clue.text: One stabbing of facial feature? Not really ear-piercing maybe!

indicators.note: the single letter pierces the word and sits inside it

parts.note: nosy read literally as 'of the nose', a facial feature
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nose piercing, which is not an ear piercing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stabbing' puts I inside NOSY. 'Not really' and 'maybe' admit the pun: ear-piercing means very loud, not a piercing in the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear-piercing sound is shrill and loud, which is what noisy describes.

clue.text: Bird in Bond film bumping off German companion

indicators.note: bumping off one thing to make room for another means a swap

parts.note: Goldfinger is the 1964 James Bond film
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A James Bond thriller in which an agent kills off his German sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off' replaces GER at the end of GOLDFINGER with CH. CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldfinch is a small European finch with a red face and yellow wing bars.

clue.text: Guarantee result will be about right

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word surrounds the letter

parts.note: to ensue is to result or follow

explanation.surface: A promise that the outcome will come out correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ENSUE round R. 'Result' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, the same as guaranteeing.

clue.text: Excavate either side of stream and river — means to get at oil maybe

definitions.text: means to get at oil maybe

indicators.note: the word for excavate is split to stand on both sides of the others

parts.note: to dig is to excavate
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Prospectors dig along both banks of a brook and a river looking for oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excavate' looks like part of the definition beside 'oil'; it is split to stand on both sides of the stream and river.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill rig is the structure that bores wells for oil or gas.
